acceptance.given: The implementation binding section and A1-A4 labels are present as authoring guidance in the frozen requirements.

oracle.expected: An artifact or validator check records binding metadata as non-normative authoring guidance and does not publish A1-A4 labels as product scope, slice IDs, or evidence identities.
forbidden: Binding metadata is treated as new product scope.
A1-A4 labels are used as published slice IDs or evidence identities.
oracle.observable: The authoring or validation artifact explicitly preserves the non-normative status of binding metadata and A1-A4 labels.

acceptance.then: The resulting contract or validation artifact preserves binding metadata as authoring-only guidance and leaves product scope and published identities unchanged.
acceptance.when: During package-plan authoring and structural validation, inspect the binding metadata interpretation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A structural contract assertion detects binding metadata or A1-A4 labels being emitted as product scope, published slice IDs, or evidence identities.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve implementation binding metadata as non-normative authoring guidance without changing product scope or published identities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only Package A authoring and validator artifacts; preserve existing skill-contract and skill-input protocols.

slice_hint.state_transition: Binding guidance is interpreted and checked as non-normative metadata while validator behavior remains scoped to declared package rules.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A structural check passes only when binding metadata and A1-A4 labels are absent from published scope and evidence identities.

acceptance.given: A local validation failure or a shared policy, schema, or validator semantic change is reported during the Package A repair lifecycle.

oracle.expected: Evidence is retained; repair scope is limited to the affected group and dependents; affected proofs are invalidated after shared semantic changes; targeted checks stabilize; the original binding identity is rebuilt and exactly one terminal replay uses that same identity.
forbidden: Unrelated groups are repaired without cause.
Affected proofs remain current after shared semantic changes.
Terminal replay occurs before affected targeted checks stabilize.
Replay uses a different or unreconstructed binding identity.
oracle.observable: The repair lifecycle record and validation sequence show retained evidence, dependency-scoped repair, proof invalidation where applicable, targeted stabilization, original-identity reconstruction, and one terminal replay.

acceptance.then: Lifecycle artifacts show retained failure evidence, affected-scope repair and invalidation, followed by targeted validation and one terminal replay with the rebuilt original binding identity.
acceptance.when: During repair orchestration after a local failure or shared semantic change, evaluate the lifecycle record and command sequence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A lifecycle check fails when evidence is discarded, unrelated groups are repaired, affected proofs are not invalidated, targeted stabilization is skipped, or terminal replay does not rebuild and reuse the original binding identity.

affected_subjects: Failure repair and proof invalidation lifecycle
slice_hint.behavior_change: Make repair orchestration preserve evidence, constrain repairs by dependency, invalidate stale proofs after shared semantic changes, rebuild the original binding identity, and order one terminal replay after targeted stabilization.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback restores prior validator lifecycle behavior without deleting historical evidence or mutating frozen requirements.

slice_hint.state_transition: A repair run moves from failure observation to scoped repair and proof invalidation, then to stabilized targeted checks and a single identity-preserving terminal replay.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The recorded lifecycle sequence contains retained evidence, affected-scope repair, required invalidation, targeted stabilization, original-identity reconstruction, and exactly one terminal replay.

acceptance.given: The four declared Package A pytest owner modules are authored for intents A01 through A25 and boundary variants.

oracle.expected: Each intent has a primary test named test_a01 through test_a25 in its declared group owner, and each boundary parameter variant has an explicit parameter ID.
forbidden: An intent lacks its named primary test case.
Boundary variants lack explicit parameter IDs.
oracle.observable: Pytest collection and source inspection expose test_a01 through test_a25 in the four declared modules and explicit IDs on boundary parameterization.

acceptance.then: The declared selectors and parameter IDs are present in the test modules and are collectable by pytest.
acceptance.when: During test-authoring validation, collect the declared modules and inspect selector names and parameter IDs.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Pytest collection or source inspection fails when any test_a01-test_a25 selector is absent from its group owner or a boundary parameter lacks an explicit ID.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Provide one named primary pytest case per intent and explicit parameter IDs for boundary variants in the declared Package A test owners.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Test selector additions are independently removable; validator production behavior and existing protocols remain compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: Declared test modules move from unbound intent declarations to collected, explicitly identified selectors.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Pytest collection and selector inspection find test_a01 through test_a25 in their owners with explicit IDs for all boundary variants.

acceptance.given: The published policy and quality schemas are supplied to the validator invocation.

oracle.expected: Validator behavior is derived from the supplied normative policy and schemas, and changing those inputs changes the applicable validation outcome or diagnostics.
forbidden: The policy or schemas are unused parallel documentation.
oracle.observable: A real validator invocation consumes the declared policy and schemas and produces structured validation behavior tied to those inputs.

acceptance.then: The validator reads and applies the normative policy and schemas as executable inputs for package validation.
acceptance.when: During a real validate_package or published CLI invocation, trace or assert policy/schema loading and input-sensitive validation behavior.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A validator integration check fails when policy or schema files are bypassed, loaded only as documentation, or do not affect validation diagnostics or results.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind validator behavior to the declared normative policy and quality schemas as actual runtime inputs.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback preserves existing owner-specific skill-contract and skill-input protocols while removing only Package A validator inputs.

slice_hint.state_transition: Validator execution transitions from static or document-only artifacts to policy- and schema-driven package validation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A real validator invocation demonstrates that declared policy and schemas are loaded and materially govern the structured result.
